question:
Circles \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) each have radius \(1.\) Circles \(A\) and \(B\) share one point of tangency. Circle \(C\) has a point of tangency with the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}.\) What is the area inside circle \(C\) but outside circle \(A\) and circle \(B?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_12A_Q11_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Subtracting the two overlap lenses from circle \(C\) reduces the problem to finding the area of one lens.

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_12A_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}\). The two equal-radius tangent circles \(A\) and \(B\) touch at \(M\), so \(AM=BM=1\). Circle \(C\) is tangent to \(\overline{AB}\) at \(M\), so its radius \(CM\) is perpendicular to \(AB\) and has length \(1\).

Complete the unit square \(AMCP\). Its fourth vertex \(P\) satisfies \(AP=CP=1\), so \(P\), like \(M\), lies on both circles \(A\) and \(C\). The angles \(\angle MAP\) and \(\angle MCP\) are both \(90^\circ\).

The chord \(MP\) divides the common lens into two circular segments. Each segment is a quarter-circle sector with a right triangle removed. The sector has area \(\pi/4\), and the triangle has perpendicular legs of length \(1\), so its area is \(1/2\). Thus one lens has area
\[
2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}-1.
\]
The same construction using \(B\) gives an equal lens. Since circles \(A\) and \(B\) touch only at \(M\), subtracting both lenses does not subtract any positive area twice. The requested area is therefore
\[
\pi-2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)=\boxed{2},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
